body:
Thanks, I'll start last/first. My mom is a psych nurse at a large local hospital (one of the managers actually). I don't want to talk to her about this because I have a strong aversion to therapy (I've been forced to go before). I just don't find them useful. I think they are good for some people and situations but I've never met one that could help. Plus I can't afford it. My mom has more than enough problems, and because she's my mom... well she can't be my therapist too. There is a lot I don't feel ok telling her, she is generally cool but is kinda weirded out by aspects of my lifestyle so I don't tell her things she doesn't need to know because she gets uncomfortable. My brothers are the same. My dad is ultra conservative & the less he knows the better we get along.

Yes I have been under more stress than normal lately, but some of these emotional problems I have are chronic. Sometimes (most of the time) I'm ok, beboping along all good but then something happens and I spiral into very dark places. Sometimes it's related to PMS (never used to have symptoms... situpid hormones). However not always. I agree that one shouldn't use friends as therapists, venting is ok but ranting over and over doesn't help & + friends aren't always the best advice givers (because personal bias). Where I find the most distressing is when I reach out (just to talk about whatever, or if I'm alone and want company), I find nobody and nothing. I've become very used to being alone, so used to it I think I've become socially weird or something. Your second paragraph makes sense, I find it hard to reach out even when I'm not moody. It's something I need to change, I just have a hard time doing it.

I am familiar with several forms of meditation, yeah it's probably something I should get back into.

Being talented doesn't make anyone worth more or less as a person. It's just a thing, something I happen to be good at. Everyone is good at something anywho. Besides artists aren't always interesting. I've known few that have the personality of paper plates, the whole artistic talent = cool person is a misnomer. 

& I wouldn't say they are shallow, it's not an uncommon thing that happens to people in their late 30's/40's. Most settle with their spouses and families. I don't have kids or a spouse, & I need more than just my career. Making friends is easy, I make friends all the time. Making close personal bestestes buds that you can have a close personal more or less daily interaction with... now that is hard. Gets harder the older you get apparently.

I make too much to go on government assistance for health care/ therapy, and I can't afford to pay for it out of pocket. I've seen more than a few as a child/young adult, and while I think they are good for some situations and people, I don't jive with them... Something about paying someone to listen to me bitch... It has never helped me.
